title: Build now, grow later

predict.q: Start: real output **1000** at full employment; price level **100**. The government spends **50** a year on roads and broadband. In the **short run**, on the SRAS curve, what happens?

options.s: Real output and the price level both rise
options.fb: The spending shifts AD right along SRAS: output 1,050, price level 105.

options.s: LRAS shifts right at once, so the price level falls
options.fb: The new capacity is not there yet. The spending shifts AD first.

options.s: Nothing happens until the roads and broadband are finished
options.fb: The money is spent while building, so AD rises straight away.

options.s: Real output rises but the price level stays at 100
options.fb: On an upward-sloping SRAS, more AD raises both output and the price level.

task: Move the **spending** slider; then switch the **time** control from "short run" to "long run".

target.do: Set spending to 50 (short run), then press Check.

takeaway: Short run (demand effect) output **1050**, price level **105**; long run, once capacity grows, output **1100** and the price level back to **100**.
